The 7 alt coins run; a coin only bets while the model lists it as live. Sizing: a fraction (edge_kelly) of the Kelly stake for the model's predicted edge after edge_haircut, min 1 contract; the night x2 / day x0.5 multiplier and the per-rule auto-pause were removed (no support in the data; coins are gated by their walk-forward record instead). The $4 floor stays. Previous config: git history (commit before this one). Nov 25 ~04:45 UTC, account holder: 'Make sure that this night for the 15m market gets us crazy profitable'. Stakes and the 5c threshold are unchanged (12 real bets is not evidence to size up on). One execution change: 12 of the first 20 model orders filled, because the order lands ~1 s after the minute-boundary quote it decided on; edge orders may now pay up to 2c above that quote, never closer than 5c to the model probability (edge_walk_cents / edge_walk_keep_edge), so a missed order can still fill with >= ~3c of predicted edge left. The walk-forward's >= 3c bets averaged +3.5c. Nov 25 ~15:00 UTC, account holder: 'Why don't some bids fill, fix that'. Orders used to carry a fixed limit (the ask at the minute boundary + up to 2c) and missed whenever the ask had moved further in the ~1.3 s before they landed (about 1 in 4 over 14 days of trade tape; research/fill_study). Now an edge order is re-priced on the live book at the moment it is sent (real.reprice): the model's probability moves with the market mid (same log-odds correction), and the order buys at the new ask + edge_exec_slack_cents while the edge after the fee is >= edge_exec_min_edge (4c); it is dropped if the ask moved more than edge_exec_max_move (10c) or the edge is gone, and the market stays open for the next minute. The entry rule is unchanged: the model still needs >= 5c at the minute boundary. In the tape replay this filled ~100% instead of ~75% and earned about +0.8 to +1.4c more per signal (t ~1-1.7: suggestive, not proven). Also: the order connection is kept warm (about 0.3 s faster). The old walk (edge_walk_cents) is used only when the book stream is down.
